newsitem.title: FRANCE: Elf, Sanofi rise on merger hopes.
newsitem.headline: Elf, Sanofi rise on merger hopes.

text.p: Shares in French pharmaceuticals company Sanofi and its parent Elf Aquitaine rose strongly on Thursday after Elf sparked merger speculation around Sanofi, traders said.
The rise in "Sanofi was obviously on the back of the Elf statement," which has raised speculation that there may be a number of companies interested, a senior equity saleswoman said.
Sanofi firmed 6.67 percent to 496 francs, while Elf climbed 2.48 percent to 446.6 at 0925 GMT.
Names of potential biders for Sanofi included Bristol Meyers Squibb, Roche and Rhone-Poulenc.
Sanofi has a distribution agreement in the United States with Bristol-Myers, while Rhone is often seen as potential candidate for spin-offs and acquisitions.
Market talk has in the past lined Roche up as a merger partner for Swedish pharmaceuticals group Astra, which Astra has denied.
